risks: No participants; the risk is a persuasive review that overstates weak evidence and changes practice for the worse.
consent: Not applicable: published work only; no new data from patients.
data: No personal data; search strategy and synthesis table archived.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: young people with learning disabilities, low health literacy, limited English or living in deprived areas may be disadvantaged by questionnaire thresholds. The review gives them a dedicated section and flags where evidence is missing.
effectiveness: Useful if the steering group revises assessment in line with what the evidence supports.
efficiency: Protected sessions and nurse specialist time only.
partnerships: Transition steering group, two young people from the youth forum, a parent representative and an adult clinician.
rebPath: No research ethics review is required for a review of published work.
limitations: Narrative selection, English only, and evidence concentrated in a few conditions.
summary: Review of published work with an equity section for disadvantaged groups.
